segments: the angel [came? {OCR?}] and said to me:
'You are the crier;
you are the truth (confirmation);
you are the camel that bears a grudge against the unbelievers;
you are the beast of burden that carries the load of the believers;
you are the Spirit;
you are John the son of Zechariah.
Preach henceforth to mankind that they should make four prostrations in their prayer:
two before the sun rises, and two before it sets,
towards Jerusalem;
saying each time these three phrases:
"God is exalted above all;
God is high over all;
God is greater than all."
And on the second day (Monday?) and on Friday let no one do any work.
And they shall fast two days in the year.
And they shall not wash excessively the reproductive organs (excretory organs {OCR?}).
And they shall not drink date wine (or beer);
but wine, as much as they wish, they may drink.
And the flesh of beasts with teeth (carnivores) alone they shall not eat.'
And when he had delivered to them such unsound and foolish doctrine,
he departed from them to Palestine,
and taught and discipled simple and rustic folk.
And from there he again vanished,
and his whereabouts has not been known again up to this day.
And in the year 1198
[1198] of the Greeks, Andrew the spatharios (spatharios,
espatharios)
went out with a large army to the territories of the Arabs; and Nazman the eunuch, the commander of the army of the Arabs, encountered him.
And the Romans were defeated,
and the Arabs snatched from them the crosses of gold and silver that were at the head of their lances.
And in the year 279
[279] of the Arabs,
al-Mu'tamid commanded
that mimes should not sit [by the waysides], nor astrologers, nor those who divine by the roadsides.
And he made the booksellers swear
not to sell books of philosophy, nor books of the controversies and disputations of the religions.
And in that same year, having drunk an excess of wine, he became intoxicated,
and suffered a stroke (or was exhausted? {OCR?}) and died,
after [reigning alongside] the son of al-Muwaffaq for nine years and nine months.
Then [al-Mu'tadid] became king in the year 279
[279] of the Arabs.
And in the year 280 {OCR? corrected from ܝܪܦ}
[280] of the Arabs, Isma'il the son of Ahmad, the general of the Arabs, invaded the territories of the Huns (Turks),
and captured their king and his wife,
and plundered his city,
and carried off about ten thousand Turkish captives,
and sheep and cattle in great abundance.
And in this year an earthquake occurred
